value: This article defines a vector space (or linear space) as a set of elements called vectors, which can be added together and scaled by numbers (scalars), adhering to a specific set of axioms. It highlights the concept's fundamental role in linear algebra, generalizing Euclidean vectors and providing a concise framework for studying linear equations. The text explores key properties such as dimension and bases, alongside related concepts like linear maps, matrices, and eigenvalues. Furthermore, it discusses various constructions (subspaces, quotients, direct sums, tensor products) and extensions to vector spaces with additional structures, including norms, inner products, and topologies (leading to normed, Banach, and Hilbert spaces), as well as algebras, vector bundles, and modules, illustrating their diverse applications in mathematics and physics.
